subject: POC Final Readout / Scheduling & Decision - Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps: Acme POC (success criteria + evaluation plan)

Hi Emma —

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for walking through your use cases and the initial architecture constraints. As promised, attached is an updated draft of the POC success criteria and the evaluation plan. Key items: 

- Success criteria (high level):
  - 90th percentile response latency < 350ms for 512-token prompts
  - Mean token cost reduction target <= $0.005/token vs current baseline
  - End-to-end throughput to support peak of 50 concurrent sessions
  - No PII leakage in logs; customer-managed KMS for keys

- Evaluation plan:
  - Week 0: Data prep & access (redwood test account + sample dataset) — Acme engineer owner: Jordan
  - Week 1–2: Model calibration & ingest test prompts — Redwood SE owner: Marcus
  - Week 3: Load testing and cost profiling — Redwood infra + Acme SRE
  - Week 4: Final readout + exec decision

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm Jordan as evaluation owner and that we have the sample dataset by EOD Fri (28 Aug).
2) Marcus to schedule a short onboarding session (30–60m) for the SE workstream.
3) Tentatively schedule the final readout (exec + technical) for the week of Sep 27 — can you confirm availability?

Attachments: POC Success Criteria v2.xlsx; Evaluation Plan - Acme.pdf

If that looks good I’ll update the timeline and send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (555) 555-0199

Marissa / Neha —

Quick technical notes and proposed onboarding agenda: 

Deployment options (for testing):
- Dedicated (recommended): 1xA100-equivalent pool, expected 95th pctl latency ~ 280–320ms for 512-token prompts with our optimized kernels; estimated token cost ~$0.0048/token with batching & KV caching enabled.
- Hosted (shared): latency will vary; not recommended for representative benchmarking.

Onboarding agenda (30–45m):
- Introductions & goals (5m)
- Access & dataset expectations (10m)
- Inference config & quantization options (10m)
- Test schedule & roles (10m)
- Q&A / next steps (5–10m)

Data requirements: sample set (100–200 canonical prompts + 50 edge cases), service account with limited S3 access, and a list of any prompt templating that touches PHI.

I’ll propose two times for the onboarding (Mon Sep 6 10:00am PT or Tue Sep 7 2:00pm PT) — will send Calendly once Emma confirms Jordan’s availability.

Attachments: none (refer to attached POC docs in the thread)

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@acme-health.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Acme POC (final readout scheduling + decision framework)

Hi team —

Thanks — Jordan confirmed he’ll send the sample dataset by Fri (28 Aug) as planned. Sep 29 works for our execs for a 30–45m readout; please send a calendar invite.

We’ve discussed internally what we need for a go/no-go:
- Go criteria (all must be met):
  - Latency: 90th pctl <= 350ms on dedicated test
  - Cost: projected unit cost within 10% of Redwood’s projected numbers
  - Security: KMS integration and no PII in logs during the test
  - Functionality: pass 90% of our golden prompts (we’ll provide list)

- If any of the above fail, our procurement team will require a follow-up plan and may push for a pilot contract with limited scope before full procurement.

For the final readout please include: 1) short technical summary (Marcus), 2) cost/ops summary (Marissa), 3) recommended contract path & next steps (Marissa + Neha).

Attachments: Decision Matrix - Exec Readout.xlsx

Next steps:
- Marissa: send calendar invite for Sep 29, 11:00am ET / 8:00am PT (we’ll confirm).
- Marcus: schedule onboarding session for Sep 6 or 7 depending on Jordan availability.
- Neha: prepare CS runbook for Week 3 load testing and what metrics we’ll present in the readout.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Emma Clarke
Director of Product | Acme Health
